title: AcropolisDocs brand registry — brand spec
description: Schema every brand.json file in references/brands/ must satisfy. Enforced by linters/lint_brand_registry.py (S rules).

name.description: The brand's name: every file's Author, Creator, Last modified by and Company (branding/scripts/doc_props.py)

owner.description: Legal owner of the brand (e.g. 'Acme Fiber, Inc.', 'AcropolisDocs')

palette.description: Two color modes — screen (dark theme default) and print (light background, deepened accents). v6.19.0: screen.bg_primary is the brand's DARK surface and print.bg_primary its LIGHT one; lint_brand_registry R1 measures that each is what its role says (white reads better than black on a dark surface), and a deck refuses `--theme dark` for a brand whose screen.bg_primary measures light.

office_family.description: v9.8.0 (L15): the family name Word and PowerPoint set for this brand's face, when the font files cannot say it themselves (their name IDs 1, 4 and 6 are blanked to '.', a web-font protection). Read by load_brand.office_family() AHEAD of each face's internal_family, then primary_family. lint_brand_fonts F3 requires it when the files' names are blank. Telekom Greece: 'TeleNeo Office'.

local_fonts.description: Font files bundled with this brand, relative to references/fonts/<slug>/. render_brand_tokens emits an @font-face per entry so the brand's real typeface reaches HTML and PDF output instead of silently falling back.

family.description: CSS family to register the file under — the brand's primary_family, not the font's own internal name, so one family carries all weights

internal_family.description: The family name in the font's own name table, recorded so the linter can verify the file is what the entry claims

web_fonts.description: Open-licence web faces for the brand's screen pages, relative to references/webfonts/<slug>/ (kept apart from references/fonts/, which the Office and PDF text measurement scans). render_brand_tokens embeds each as a base64 @font-face in screen mode only, so a page asks no outside host for a font (v11.24.0, SEC-5) and the PDF, which renders through fontconfig, is unchanged.

weight.description: the variable face's weight range, e.g. "100 900"

assets.description: Per-brand BINARY assets that are the brand owner's own property, shipped alongside the token data. Declared here rather than discovered by a filesystem probe so that resolution matches every other brand property, the build can derive what to package from the declaration, and a declared-but-absent file is a hard packaging error instead of a silent fallback. Absent key = no asset = the generic path (theme injection for the deck template), which is a legitimate, declared state.

pptx_template.description: The brand's own PowerPoint template. build_deck.resolve_template() uses it verbatim (footer mode 'mark_only') instead of theme-injecting the AcropolisDocs base.

file.description: Filename relative to skills/pptx/assets/templates/. The stem must equal the brand slug — prune() scopes per-brand binaries by the slug in front of the first dot.

layouts_sidecar.description: Optional <slug>.layouts.json beside the template, required when the template's own layout NAMES match none of pptxutil.classify_layout's markers. Travels with the template as one unit.

layout_count.description: Slide layouts the template carries, recorded so the linter can verify the file is what the entry claims — the deck-template analogue of local_fonts.internal_family.

logo.description: Brand logo SVGs as inline strings. dark = for dark backgrounds (light fills), light = for light backgrounds (dark fills): the keys name the GROUND each mark is drawn on, never the colour of the mark itself. A mark that carries its own panel may register one SVG under both. v6.19.0: lint_brand_registry measures each on the surface its key names (palette.screen.bg_primary for `dark`, palette.print.bg_primary for `light`) as a mark, 3:1 - L1 FAILS a pair registered the wrong way round, L2 warns when no registered mark reads on a surface - and every consumer takes the variant for the ground it draws on (a deck canvas, a page theme, a PDF cover or masthead).

dark.description: Full SVG markup including <svg ...> ... </svg>: the mark drawn on a DARK ground. Where the brand's own file documents a dark-ground treatment (RADCOM's `.logo-transform { fill: #FFFFFF }`), this is the file with that treatment applied.

light.description: Full SVG markup: the mark drawn on a LIGHT ground.

prohibited.description: Marketing terms / claims the brand forbids

ip_rules.description: Trademark / IP guardrails the brand requires

naming_overrides.description: Optional overrides for AcropolisDocs file-naming convention

accept_prefixes.description: v8.4.0: prefixes name_check.validate() also passes, without being written. For a client folder whose house convention differs from the prefix the plugin writes.

accreditation.description: Universal accreditation credit (home brand only). Single source for the accreditation every deliverable carries regardless of active brand: `text`/`full` on paper, in Word, decks, workbooks and Markdown; `html_label` linked to `href` beside the mark in every HTML footer (v11.9.0).

html_label.description: v11.9.0: the words of the HTML footer's lockup, beside the tiny mark, as a link to `href`. Every HTML page; the PDF band, Word, PowerPoint, xlsx and the Markdown bundle keep `text` / `full`.

href.description: v11.9.0: where the HTML lockup's `html_label` links (an absolute https URL).

locale.description: v9.8.0 (SPEC_telekom-greece L2): the language this brand's deliverables are written in. Resolved by skills/branding/scripts/doc_locale.py, the one owner (locale_sites.site_lang applies it): the run's --lang or spec['lang'] wins, then the source page's own non-English lang, then locale.default, then 'en'. A language outside locale.supported is refused at the CLI's entry. A brand with no locale block writes English, unchanged.

default.description: The language a deliverable is written in when nobody asks for one.

supported.description: Languages this brand may be written in; must contain default. lint_brand_fonts F6 requires every declared face to carry the script of each supported language.

strings.description: Per-language brand strings, keyed by language then field (e.g. {"el": {"tagline": "..."}}). A field absent for a language falls back to the identity field.

accent_1.description: Primary brand accent (H1/H2, table headers, CTA)

sequential.description: STORED single-hue ramp, light to dark, anchored on accent_1, for many-category part-to-whole fills where the five positional slots run out. Written at ingest by normalize_brand.py. Stored rather than computed at render time because palette_guard allowlists DECLARED data: a ramp derived while rendering is on-brand by construction and off-allowlist by definition, and blocked 10 of 12 brand/substrate pairs under --strict when it was tried (v4.27.0). The v4.26.0 `series.categorical` container that used to sit here is gone — accent_1..accent_5 ARE the series.

bg_primary.description: The surface this mode's slides and pages are drawn on: in `screen` the brand's DARK surface, in `print` its light one. v6.19.0: measured against its role (lint_brand_registry R1); a screen value that is light registers no dark surface, and a deck says so rather than drawing a white deck and calling it dark.

bg_accent.description: v6.18.0 - the brand's ACCENT SURFACE: the background a deck's `alt` theme is drawn on. Declared, never derived: palette_guard admits tints toward it only because it is registered here, and build_deck refuses `--theme alt` for a brand that declares none. Read from screen first, then print.

series.description: Per-brand authored chart series ramp. v4.84.0: load_brand's resolve_series() 'authored' branch, resolve_sequential() step 1 and _validate_series() have consumed this since it was written, but additionalProperties:false meant NO schema-valid brand could declare it — injecting it raised "Additional properties are not allowed ('series' was unexpected)" and resolve_series fell back to the positional slots. The escape hatch documented in the fork/brand spec was unreachable and _validate_series was dead code.
